entries.remark: Work done by an external force in moving a charge q from R to P against the electric field. It is independent of the path taken.
Work done per unit test charge in bringing it from infinity to a point. Scalar quantity.

entries.quantity: Potential due to a Point Charge
entries.remark: Potential decreases as 1/r. It is positive for positive charges and negative for negative charges.

entries.quantity: Potential due to an Electric Dipole
entries.remark: Potential falls off as 1/r² at large distances. It is zero on the equatorial plane (θ = 90°).
A surface where potential is the same at every point. No work is done moving a charge on this surface. Electric field is always perpendicular to it.
Electric field is in the direction of steepest decrease of potential. Its magnitude is the potential gradient.
The electric field inside a cavity of a conductor is zero. This protects sensitive instruments from external electrical noise.
The ability of a system to store charge. Unit is Farad (F). Depends on geometry and the medium between conductors.
Capacitance for two plates of area A separated by distance d. If a dielectric (K) is added, C becomes K * C₀.
Charge Q is the same on each capacitor. Potential V is divided.
Potential V is the same across each. Charge Q is divided.
Energy is stored in the electric field between the plates.
Non-conducting substances that develop a net dipole moment in an external electric field, reducing the internal field.
